source_caption:
One of the most beautiful films from Sir Mike Flanagan! 

This movie concept describes a reverse-chronological story. It begins with the end of a man's life and moves backward through middle age to childhood to reveal his inner universe. The powerful metaphor of a dying person being like a burning library comes from writer Kurt Vonnegut, who famously quoted Walt Whitman's sentiment about containing multitudes.

The Life of Chuck (2024) and The Shawshank Redemption (1994) both feature recurring images of actress Rita Hayworth. The latter film features clips and footage from Gilda (1946), and this film showcases clip from Cover Girl (1944). Both movies are also based on novellas written by Stephen King.

source_details.title: The Life of Chuck
source_details.synopsis: The Life of Chuck is a 2024 American fantasy drama film written for the screen, co-produced, edited, and directed by Mike Flanagan. It is based on the 2020 novella of the same name by Stephen King. The film stars Tom Hiddleston, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Karen Gillan, Mia Sara, Carl Lumbly, Benjamin Pajak, Jacob Tremblay, and Mark Hamill, with narration by Nick Offerman. The film's plot follows the formative moments in the life of Charles "Chuck" Krantz, chronicled in reverse chronological order, from his death (and the "end of the universe" contained within it) to his childhood.
